question: Should Gateway origin policy allow scheme-level extension wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes what constrained grammar or config surface should own that trust?
rationale: This changes the Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary and the current config contract treats `allowedOrigins` as exact full origins except for the global `*`, so automation should not choose the permanent wildcard grammar or trust model.

options.title: Approve constrained extension patterns
options.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit positive and negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Advance exact custom-scheme origin fixes and accept that changing Chrome extension IDs remain an operator config task.

options.title: Reject extension-wide trust
options.body: Document that trusting every Chrome extension origin is too broad for Gateway origin authorization and keep `chrome-extension://*` unsupported.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension patterns
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit positive and negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history-backed connection to the Gateway origin security boundary and config policy.
